title: A binary-input channel has the same fixed-prior Umegaki SDPI constant with any finite quantum reference
status_authority: The exact source scope and version-bound receiving review are recorded below; this card does not certify priority, physical operation, or practical advantage.
reported_status: The recipient checked the selected source passages and the cited published ingredient at the exact scope below. No full-package audit, separate binary producer audit, producer-script replay, external priority review, or physical/practical validation is asserted.

proof_availability.classification_scope: For every finite-output classical channel T with binary input and every full-support fixed prior pi, let K=A_0+A_1, Y_y=T_{y0}A_0+T_{y1}A_1, and q_y=(T pi)_y. For arbitrary positive A_0,A_1 on any common finite-dimensional quantum reference, sum_{y:q_y>0} D(Y_y || q_y K) <= eta(T,pi) sum_{i=0}^1 D(A_i || pi_i K), where eta(T,pi) is the scalar fixed-prior Umegaki SDPI constant. Scalar references give the matching lower bound, so allowing an arbitrary finite quantum reference does not change this fixed-prior constant. Boundary: This fixes the binary transmitted alphabet and the prior. It is not the global-prior binary coefficient in N970, not an arbitrary-alphabet theorem with arbitrary references, not a reduction of multi-symbol quantum-memory problems, and not a t log t matrix-SDPI separation.
